findings.claim: The requirement to honour MessagePack attributes already present on T is neither implemented nor tested. When no surrogate is supplied, the collector always builds contractless members, and every external-type fixture is deliberately attribute-free, so the tests cannot detect ignored [MessagePackObject]/[Key] contracts.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an external type annotated with [MessagePackObject] and non-consecutive integer [Key] values plus an [IgnoreMember] property, generate its formatter without SurrogateType, and assert the array header, round-trip values, and ignored member. The current contractless implementation should emit a string-keyed map instead and fail the test.

findings.claim: The explicit bodyless-declaration acceptance criterion has no test: all new formatter declarations use brace bodies. A regression specific to 'partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;' would therefore go unnoticed.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator test whose only formatter declaration is '[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class MyFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<MyType>;' and verify that generation completes without MsgPack019 or compiler errors and supplies Serialize/Deserialize.

findings.claim: Public-field serialization in contractless mode is untested because ExternalPerson, ExternalPoint, and ExternalWidget expose only properties. The field arm of IsPublicReadWrite can stop accepting fields without failing any new test.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:280 negate-condition: field.DeclaredAccessibility == Accessibility.Public && !field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst -> false; expected to survive because no external fixture declares a public instance field.

findings.claim: No negative test covers duplicate surrogate keys, so removal of the uniqueness guard is not detected despite the risk of generating an invalid or ambiguous wire contract.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:199 remove-guard: if (!claimedKeys.Add(key)) { report KeysMustBeUnique; return null; } -> remove the complete block; expected to survive because all test surrogates use unique keys and no test expects MsgPack006 for a surrogate.

findings.claim: Surrogate members without a valid integer or string [Key] are not tested. Existing negative cases all have a valid key and fail later on member matching or mixed key kinds, leaving the MemberNeedsKey guard uncovered.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:170 remove-guard: if (key is not (int or string)) { report MemberNeedsKey; return null; } -> remove the complete block; expected to survive because no test surrogate has an unkeyed, non-ignored member or an invalid key argument type.

findings.claim: The accessible parameterless-constructor requirement has no negative test. Removing its guard survives because all successful fixtures have implicit public parameterless constructors.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:75 remove-guard: if (isClass && !type.InstanceConstructors.Any(c => c.Parameters.Length == 0 && compilation.IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(c, formatter))) { report NoDeserializingConstructor; return null; } -> remove the complete guard; expected to survive because no test formatter targets a class lacking an accessible parameterless constructor.
